findings.issue_text: Abstract sync_assignee_outbound in issues.py and concrete provider implementations (Jira, GitHub, GitLab, etc.) don't accept the new assignment_source parameter, causing TypeError when the task calls it with that kwarg; tests mask this via mocks

sync_status_outbound gained an assignment_source parameter that no call site populates, creating dead surface and falsely implying status cycles are handled
test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign was edited into a formatting-only no-op diff while its body was duplicated into the new matching-source test, creating drifting duplicated test setup

`to_dict()` embeds a raw datetime object in Celery task kwargs, causing kombu's JSON serializer to raise EncodeError and `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(...)` to fail whenever assignment_source is present, stopping inbound-triggered assignment propagation to other linked integrations
`from_dict` reconstructs the dataclass via `cls(**input_dict)` without type validation, so fields like integration_id can arrive as a string/bool/float after crossing the task-queue boundary
Unvalidated integration_id types cause the cycle-prevention check comparing str to int to silently evaluate False, bypassing the sync-cycle guard and re-opening the infinite A↔B sync loop

Missing test coverage for the cycle-prevention guard's mismatched-integration path: no test creates an AssignmentSource with a different integration_id and asserts sync_assignee_outbound is still called, so a regression returning False for any non-None sync_source would pass the test suite while killing cross-integration propagation

No test exercises the full inbound-to-outbound assignment round-trip (external event → sync_group_assignee_inbound → GroupAssignee.assign with assignment_source → outbound task suppression), so breaks in AssignmentSource.from_integration or the plumbing from inbound sync to the task would ship undetected

assert_not_called() is a weak negative assertion in the suppression test: it cannot distinguish 'suppressed by cycle guard' from 'task failed or never dispatched for an unrelated reason'; a positive control (different integration → mock IS called) is needed

assignment_source.to_dict() puts a raw datetime ('queued') into Celery apply_async kwargs, which raises EncodeError at enqueue time under the default JSON serializer, causing every inbound-sourced assignment to fail rather than sync
AssignmentSource.from_dict does not validate the 'queued' field type, so a JSON-decoded string silently constructs a malformed AssignmentSource with a string instead of datetime
sync_status_outbound's signature gained an assignment_source parameter but no implementation, caller, or test passes a non-None value to it, leaving the new contract parameter behaviorally unverified

Class-level default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` in assignment_source.py is evaluated once at module import, so every AssignmentSource instance gets a stale process-start timestamp rather than actual queue time
If `from_dict` reconstitutes a message serialized without `queued`, the value is the stale import-time default, silently misdating the event
Mutable/evaluated-once dataclass defaults are a drift trap: a future field with a computed default will silently backfill from a stale snapshot on the `cls(**input_dict)` deserialization path

`to_dict()` uses `asdict()` leaving `queued` as a raw datetime, which fails under JSON-serialized Celery kwargs so `sync_assignee_outbound` is never delivered, silently stopping outward assignment sync

On the consuming side, if `queued` arrives as an ISO string after a JSON round-trip, `cls(**input_dict)` raises TypeError and `from_dict` returns None, bypassing the `should_sync` cycle guard and re-enabling the sync loop

`from_dict` swallowing ValueError/TypeError to None means schema drift degrades to 'no source recorded' rather than an error, re-enabling the sync loop with no log line anywhere, especially during rolling deploys with interleaved old/new format tasks
queued field default `timezone.now()` is evaluated at class-definition (import) time, so every instance carries the process-start timestamp rather than actual queue time
datetime in queued field cannot be serialized by Celery's default JSON serializer, causing EncodeError when passed to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async kwargs
from_dict swallows malformed payloads by returning None, which silently disables the sync-cycle guard and can recreate the sync loop this PR exists to prevent
Inbound assign path drops assignment_source when user_id is None, causing later legitimate reassignments to be wrongly suppressed by should_sync's integration-id match
queued field is dead weight: nothing reads it and deleting it (leaving only source_name and integration_id) would eliminate the non-JSON-native serialization failure surface

adjudication_records.issue_text: Abstract sync_assignee_outbound in issues.py and concrete provider implementations (Jira, GitHub, GitLab, etc.) don't accept the new assignment_source parameter, causing TypeError when the task calls it with that kwarg; tests mask this via mocks

adjudication.rationale: The diff updates the Celery task to call `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` (in `sync_assignee_outbound.py`), but in `issues.py` only `sync_status_outbound`’s abstract signature is updated to accept `assignment_source`; the abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` definition is present but not updated in this diff. That means any concrete integration installation method that doesn’t accept `assignment_source` (or generic `**kwargs`) will raise a `TypeError` at runtime. The updated tests patch/mocks `ExampleIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound`, so they would not catch a real signature mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apply_async with assignment_source.to_dict() containing a raw datetime fails at enqueue time with kombu JSON serialization EncodeError, so inbound-triggered assignee syncs never run

AssignmentSource dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates once at class definition time, so all instances share an import-time timestamp; should use field(default_factory=timezone.now)
matched_golden_ids: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same dataclass default-value pitfall: `timezone.now()` is evaluated at class definition/import time, causing all instances to share the same timestamp, and suggests using `default_factory`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict only catches (ValueError, TypeError) and doesn't convert ISO string back to datetime, so deserialized queued field is a str contradicting the declared type; also no kwargs-filter means extra keys silently parse to None, discarding the cycle-prevention signal

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s `AssignmentSource.from_dict` simply does `cls(**input_dict)` and returns `None` on `TypeError`/`ValueError`. That means **extra keys do not “silently parse to None”**; they cause a `TypeError` and the whole object becomes `None`. Also, the diff does not show any ISO-string serialization of `queued`: `to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)`, which will keep `queued` as a `datetime` object, and `queued` is not used in the cycle-prevention check (only `integration_id` is). So the claimed datetime-string contradiction and loss of “cycle-prevention signal” via extra keys are not directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` dataclass field default is evaluated once at import time, so every AssignmentSource instance carries the process-start timestamp instead of the actual enqueue time, and the to_dict test passes vacuously

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` the field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` at class definition/import time, so the default becomes a single fixed `datetime` reused for all instances that don’t explicitly pass `queued`. In a dataclass this should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to compute per-instance. The test `test_to_dict` only asserts `queued` is not None, which would pass even with a constant timestamp, so it wouldn’t catch the bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `to_dict()` output contains a raw `datetime` in Celery task kwargs, which crashes `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` with `EncodeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable` at enqueue time, breaking the happy path
matched_golden_ids: to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same core issue: `to_dict()` includes a raw `datetime` (for `queued`) that, when used in Celery task kwargs (via `apply_async`), can fail JSON serialization and cause enqueue-time errors (e.g., `EncodeError`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test verifies the cross-integration propagation (assignment from integration A syncing outward to integration B) that the new code comment promises; a regression inverting the comparison or comparing on source_name instead of integration_id would pass the test suite

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` to block outbound sync only when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (to prevent cycles). Tests cover the blocking case (`test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration`) and the default `None` case, but there is no test asserting the opposite behavior: when `assignment_source` is present and refers to a *different* integration, outbound sync still occurs. A regression that inverts the comparison or uses `source_name` instead of `integration_id` could still pass the current suite because only the “same integration -> don’t sync” branch is explicitly exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cycle prevention is wired for assignee only; the status-sync loop on the same inbound→outbound machinery is untouched, so a resolve echo loop between systems remains and `sync_status_outbound`'s `assignment_source` parameter has no caller (dead weight or missing wiring)

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, cycle-prevention via `AssignmentSource` is only threaded through the assignee outbound path (GroupAssignee.assign/deassign -> `sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> task `sync_assignee_outbound` -> `installation.should_sync(..., parsed_assignment_source)`). Although `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` now accepts `sync_source` and blocks same-integration propagation, and `sync_status_outbound` gained an `assignment_source` parameter, there are no changes shown that pass an `AssignmentSource` into any status-sync entrypoints/tasks. So within the changed code, status sync does not benefit from the new cycle-prevention plumbing, and the added `assignment_source` arg on `sync_status_outbound` is not wired up by any caller in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `assignment_source` param is only threaded through the `assignee_type == "user"` and default outbound branches in `GroupAssignee.assign`/`deassign`; existing callers (auto-assign via GroupOwner, escalations, etc.) pass no source, so `assignment_source=None` bypasses the cycle check and can reopen sync loops

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an optional `assignment_source` that is specifically meant to be provided when an assignee change originates from an integration, so `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` can suppress outbound sync back to the same integration. The only integration-originated path shown here (`sync_group_assignee_inbound`) now passes `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` into `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign`, which then threads it through to `sync_group_assignee_outbound` and the Celery task. Other existing callers (auto-assign, escalations, etc.) passing `assignment_source=None` will still sync outbound, but that does not imply a sync loop because those changes are not shown to originate from the target integration. The claim that this “can reopen sync loops” is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter that no caller, implementation, or requirement in the diff traces to — speculative API surface that silently does nothing

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the abstract method signature `sync_status_outbound(..., assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None, **kwargs)` in `IssueSyncIntegration` (issues.py), but there are no corresponding call-site changes or any logic in this diff that passes/consumes `assignment_source` for status syncing (unlike assignee syncing, where it’s plumbed through tasks and used in `should_sync`). This adds API surface that is currently unused within the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The sync-cycle prevention guard (sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id) is only applied in the assignee path, not the status or comments paths, under-scoping the stated cross-system sync-cycle prevention intent

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, the new sync-cycle guard lives in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` and checks `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`. However, the only call site updated here to *pass* a source is the assignee outbound task (`sync_assignee_outbound` parses `assignment_source_dict` and calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`). While `sync_status_outbound`’s signature is extended to accept `assignment_source`, this diff does not show any corresponding wiring that passes a source into `should_sync` for status (or any comments sync path). So, based on the diff alone, the cycle-prevention behavior is effectively applied only to the assignee flow unless other (unshown) call sites were also updated elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: assignment_source.to_dict() emits a datetime 'queued' field passed as kwargs to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async, causing Celery JSON serializer EncodeError so every inbound-triggered assignee sync fails to enqueue

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource`, `to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)`, which includes the `queued: datetime` field. `sync_group_assignee_outbound()` passes this dict into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={... "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})`. A plain `datetime` in task kwargs is not JSON-serializable under Celery’s common JSON serializer, so enqueuing can fail with an encode error when `assignment_source` is provided (inbound-triggered outbound sync path).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'queued' field in assignment_source is untraceable to any requirement — nothing reads it

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` (new file), the `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` field is serialized via `to_dict()` (used when enqueueing `sync_assignee_outbound` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`) and deserialized in `from_dict()`, but within this diff nothing ever reads/uses `queued` (only `integration_id` is checked in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync`, and `source_name` isn’t referenced either). This makes the field currently redundant overhead, though not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dataclass default queued: datetime = timezone.now() is evaluated at class-definition time, so every instance gets a frozen process-start timestamp instead of enqueue time

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`, the dataclass defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. This calls `timezone.now()` at class definition/import time, so all `AssignmentSource` instances created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp (process start) rather than the creation/enqueue time. In dataclasses this should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to get a fresh value per instance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groupassign.py (core region-silo model) imports from sentry.integrations.services.assignment_source at module scope, creating a models→integrations-services layering dependency

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a module-scope import in the core region-silo model `src/sentry/models/groupassignee.py`: `from sentry.integrations.services.assignment_source import AssignmentSource`. This creates a direct dependency from `sentry.models` to `sentry.integrations.services`, which is an architecture/layering concern (and could increase risk of circular imports or cross-layer coupling), even if it doesn’t immediately break runtime behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: should_sync signature changed to accept sync_source but only IssueSyncIntegration's override handles it; other subclasses overriding should_sync(self, attribute) will raise TypeError with the new calling convention, and no tests verify compatibility

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the calling convention: `sync_assignee_outbound` now calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` (tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py), and the base `IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync` signature was updated accordingly. While `IssueSyncIntegration` was updated too, the diff does not show whether other `IntegrationInstallation` subclasses override `should_sync(self, attribute)` without accepting the new optional parameter; if any do, this new call pattern would raise `TypeError`. This is a concrete compatibility risk created by the diff, but the presence of such subclasses is not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupAssignee.objects.assign(self.group, self.user,) reformatted to multi-line with no argument change — diff-noise-only edit obscuring the actual behavioral change in the hunk

adjudication.rationale: The cited change in `tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py` does reformat `GroupAssignee.objects.assign(self.group, self.user)` into a multi-line call, but this is a trivial style-only adjustment inside a hunk that also makes substantive, review-relevant changes (e.g., new `assignment_source` plumbing and updated mock assertions expecting `assignment_source=None`). Calling this out as a meaningful review finding is effectively a pure formatting nit rather than a concrete diff-grounded issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: kwarg assignment_source passed to sync_assignee_outbound whose signature was never updated, causing TypeError and breaking cross-system sync

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* update the Celery task `sync_assignee_outbound` signature to accept `assignment_source_dict` (not `assignment_source`) and `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes that kwarg accordingly. There is no place in the shown diff where `assignment_source` is passed to the task without a matching parameter, so the claimed `TypeError` from an unupdated task signature is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw datetime in Celery task kwargs via assignment_source.to_dict() is not JSON serializable, causing EncodeError/TypeError at dispatch

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` which returns `asdict(self)` including `queued: datetime` (default `timezone.now()`) from `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`. That dict is passed directly into Celery task kwargs as `assignment_source_dict` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound()` (`apply_async(kwargs={... "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})`). A raw `datetime` inside kwargs is not JSON-serializable under Celery/Kombu’s JSON serializer, so dispatch can raise an EncodeError/TypeError. The new test even asserts `queued` is present, reinforcing that a datetime will be included.

adjudication_records.issue_text: queued default datetime evaluated once at class-definition time instead of per instance; should use field(default_factory=timezone.now)

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` (new file `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`), the dataclass defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. This calls `timezone.now()` at import/class-definition time, so all instances created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp. To get a per-instance timestamp it should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict returning None on parse errors re-enables sync cycle instead of safe no-op, enabling infinite echo assign loop

adjudication.rationale: The new anti-sync-cycle guard in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync()` only blocks outbound sync when a valid `AssignmentSource` is present and its `integration_id` matches (`if sync_source and sync_source.integration_id == ...: return False`). In `sync_assignee_outbound`, `AssignmentSource.from_dict()` returns `None` on any parse error, which then bypasses this guard and proceeds with outbound sync (`installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`). So a malformed/failed-to-parse `assignment_source_dict` could defeat the cycle-prevention logic. The diff does not prove such parse errors will occur in practice (the code usually passes `to_dict()`), so this is an edge-case robustness concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cycle guard only blocks self-echo between same integration, not two-integration ping-pong loops, lacking idempotency or convergence checks

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a guard in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` that only skips syncing when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (i.e., prevents echoing back to the same integration). The comment explicitly says this “should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward.” Nothing in the diff adds broader cycle detection/idempotency across multiple integrations, so a potential A↔B ping-pong loop is not addressed by this change. Whether that loop actually occurs depends on behavior outside the diff, so it’s more of a scope/architecture gap than a verifiable defect here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: assignment_source invariant enforced only by convention at each assign/deassign call site; callers not threading the source silently re-open echo cycle

adjudication.rationale: The loop-prevention logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync()` only triggers when a non-None `sync_source`/`assignment_source` is provided (`if sync_source and sync_source.integration_id == ...: return False`). But `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign` and `sync_group_assignee_outbound` make `assignment_source` optional with a default of `None`, so existing callers that don’t thread it will still enqueue outbound sync with `assignment_source_dict=None` and bypass the cycle check. The diff updates one inbound path (`sync_group_assignee_inbound`) to pass `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)`, but the invariant is not enforced centrally and depends on call-site discipline.

adjudication_records.issue_text: queued: datetime = timezone.now() in AssignmentSource is evaluated at import time, not per-instance, so every instance carries a stale process-import timestamp

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` (new file `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`), the dataclass field is defined as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. This calls `timezone.now()` at class definition/import time, so all instances created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp. Dataclasses require `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to evaluate per-instance, so the finding correctly identifies a real defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: to_dict() puts a raw datetime into Celery apply_async kwargs, which fails to serialize under a JSON-configured broker (TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable)

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource`, `queued` is a `datetime` defaulting to `timezone.now()` and `to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)`, which will include that raw `datetime` object (see `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`). That dict is then passed directly into Celery task kwargs via `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(..., kwargs={..., "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})` in `src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py`. If Celery is configured to use JSON serialization for task messages, this payload will not be JSON-serializable and can raise `TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict returns None on parse failure, silently disabling cycle suppression with no logging

That said, within this diff the only shown producer is `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` (which supplies an int) and Celery JSON serialization typically preserves numeric types, so the str-vs-int scenario isn’t demonstrably occurring from the shown changes.
